ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$7.17 (voucher) for the 5.09 km unexempted detour on this RydeTAXI metered trip, per RD-2 (unexempted extra_km × distance_fare ÷ distance_km = 5.09 × 1.4101); record the RD-1 shortest-route breach and send the driver's account to Ryde review as a repeat route-deviation offender "+ flag_account".
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat, complaint and driver statement contain no threat, abuse, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation → safety_concern "none". Dispute type is route_deviation, not safety.

Trip facts: RydeTAXI (metered), Buona Vista MRT → Pasir Ris MRT. Quoted route 27.363 km / 38 min; meter shows 29.82 km (fare.distance_km), total S$59.88, distance fare S$42.05 (unit rate = 42.05 ÷ 29.82 = S$1.4101/km), waiting 0.11 (metered minutes), no tolls, no edit-destination fee. Trip ran 18:11:00–18:58:55 (≈48 min).

Detour measurement: I matched the (thinned, 30 s) GPS trace against the quoted polyline. The trace departs the quoted corridor at ≈18:32:50 (1.3242, 103.8961) and follows a loop east through Tampines (18:33–18:42) that the quoted route does not take, rejoining the corridor at ≈18:43–18:44 (1.3241, 103.9272). Straight-line geometry of that loop is ≈5.5 km vs ≈0.5 km of quoted route replaced → extra ≈5.0 km, consistent with the independent meter excess: 29.82 − 27.363 = 2.457 km greater than the pre-loop excess at 18:32 (≈30.20 km driven vs ≈29.29 km quoted to that point, i.e. the driver was already ≈0.9 km longer than the quote), with the remainder concentrated in the loop. I take extra_km ≈ 5.09, which reproduces the whole meter excess as one unexempted segment (a single segment, so no residue from un-attributed jitter).

Consent (RD-5): the only chat is at 18:35:15/18:35:55 — after the detour began (≈18:32:50) — so it is not consent "before the deviation" for that segment; the driver's statement that the rider agreed verbally is a claim, not consent (G11). What was said is in any case a general routing authorisation ("随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间"), which covers a route chosen to reach the destination but not a driver's own loop; the driven loop is a diversion that reaches no destination and the record places it away from where the rider was (already inside the loop area at Tampines when the driver asked). The rider's follow-up "我不觉得那条路更快" disputes the loop. Ground = driver_errand / consent_after_or_none → counts, no exemption. RD-4 is not available: the PIE speed-band (band 2) doesn't cover the detoured segment and, alone, cannot exempt (RD-4(b)); no incidents.

Arithmetic (RD-2, RydeTAXI): refund = 5.09 km × 1.4101 = S$7.1777 → S$7.18 (state S$7.18; stated amount rounded to the cent). Waiting time is meter-accrued and not refundable (RD-3(c)); no non-metered add-ons.

RD-6: refund > 0 and driver.route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 (≥1) → this case makes the pattern "repeated"; flag_account applies (profile used only for the additional action, not to establish the deviation).

Evidence: GPS present and complete for the trip (5 s grid, thinned ×6), chat timestamped, meter and quoted route both available → sufficient. One caveat: the "Jam on PIE is building up" line is not corroborated by any traffic incident on the detoured segment (incidents empty; band 2 not band 1), which is why RD-4 does not exempt.

segment_findings.reason: Driver left the quoted route at ≈18:32:50 to loop east through Tampines (rejoining ≈18:43); the only chat is at 18:35:15/18:35:55, i.e. after the deviation began, so no rider message precedes it (RD-5). The words are a general routing authorisation ("whichever way is faster"), which does not cover a diversion that reaches no destination; at the time of asking the driver was already inside the loop, so no consent can attach to a request not yet made. No traffic incident and no covering band 1/2 on the replaced corridor → RD-4 unavailable. extra_km ≈ 5.09, not exempted → counts under RD-1/RD-2 with refund 5.09 × (42.05 ÷ 29.82) = S$7.18.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver claims the rider agreed verbally to any faster way; a verbal agreement reported only in the driver's statement is a claim, not consent (G11), and the written chat he relies on is timestamped after the deviation began (RD-5). Not accepted.

Driver relies on building traffic on PIE; no traffic incident exists on the replaced corridor (incidents empty) and the only relevant band record is band 2, which under RD-4(b) is corroborative only and cannot exempt on its own. Not accepted as a reasonable cause.
